approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the unsigned Wine Spires pullout on SR-20 near milepost 166 (~4,300 ft)

pins.name: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout (milepost 166)
pins.note: Unmarked highway pullout ~2-4 miles east of the Washington Pass hairpin turn; climbers descend to Early Winters Creek then switchback up to Burgundy Col.
pins.directions: Drive SR-20 to the unsigned pullout near milepost 166, roughly four miles east of Washington Pass, at about 4,300 ft. There is no sign and no developed trailhead here, only a broad shoulder pullout, so watch your odometer. Check WSDOT before travelling: the highway is gated shut through the winter and reopens somewhere between mid-April and late June depending on snowpack and slide repair.

pins.name: Burgundy Creek bench camp — west side
Burgundy Col
pins.directions: From the pullout, drop off the highway on a steep, faint boot path and descend the talus to Early Winters Creek, crossing on logs. Climb the far side on the climber's path, switchbacking up talus benches and loose cairned gullies through timber and boulders; where the boot track braids, stay climber's-left, keeping north of the drainage coming down from the basin below the spires, and aim for the obvious notch of the col. It is about 3,500 ft of gain and 3-4 hours with an overnight pack, and snow can linger in the gully below the col into July, so carry an axe early in the season.

pins.name: Chianti Spire / East Face (Rebel Yell) area
pins.directions: Drop off the col down a short snow and rock step and traverse south beneath the east face of Burgundy Spire, crossing a small snowy rib onto the upper Silver Star Glacier, then around to the obvious east side of Chianti Spire at about 7,900 ft. Reckon on under an hour from the col, or from the larch bench camp lower down. Carry an ice axe through midsummer, as the rib and the glacier margin are often firm or icy first thing in the morning.

pins.name: Chianti Spire Summit
pins.directions: Seven pitches of gear-protected crack climbing up the east face, four to six hours for most parties. Start up flakes into the obvious wide dihedral, taking either the easier right-hand start or the thinner left-hand finger crack, which rejoins by the top of pitch 1, then the offwidth and the lower-angle dihedral above, then the balancy blind step left across the arete past a fixed bolt on pitch 4. Pitch 5 is the technical crux, a sustained thin-hands crack widening through cupped hands to fists and capped by a strenuous offwidth move, and pitch 6 follows the same system to a rising ramp trending left to the exposed summit block, gained by short final moves past a single bolt.
